about:
Candidate voices for the two announcers. design.py speaks each announcer's ref_text in every candidate and saves voices/<candidate>.flac; render.py clones the 'chosen' one for every line, and the clone copies that clip's delivery as well as its voice, so the ref_text is written as live, high-energy television sports commentary. A candidate is a plain-English description for Qwen3-TTS VoiceDesign ('instruct'), or another candidate's voice cloned onto this announcer's ref_text ('clone', by the Base model). A candidate may speak its own 'ref_text' instead of the announcer's, and may set 'max_pause_s' to tighten internal pauses in the reference clip. 'seed' picks the take.

History & Qwen3-TTS tuning notes:
1. First pass (2026-10-16, dani-jersey and wren-light): designed reading relaxed radio DJ copy; every cloned line came out sounding like a sleepy late-night FM host.
2. Second pass (2026-10-18, dani-booth and wren-booth): tried VoiceDesign with 'excited broadcaster' + exclamation marks on every sentence, which caused Qwen3-TTS VoiceDesign to jump an octave into a 380-450 Hz cheerleader archetype (0.4-0.8 similar to midnight-playground's Kit). Worked around it by cloning dani-jersey and wren-light onto excited ref_text, then cloning those clones a second time in render.py. However, double-cloning washed out Dani's smoky 227 Hz voice into a flat 283 Hz narrator voice, made Dani and Wren sound too alike (283 Hz vs 264 Hz), and ended ref_text on a calm falling transition ('Here comes the next rider out of the gate...'), which due to causal self-attention recency bias in Base ICL cloning made short action calls start at low energy.
3. Third pass (2026-10-24, dani-pipe and wren-crisp): designed directly with VoiceDesign (no double-cloning) using three key Qwen3-TTS rules:
   - Ground register in 'instruct', not exclamation marks: asking for 'loud / shouting / excited' with '!' on every sentence collapses VoiceDesign into high-F0 screaming. Instead, anchor Dani in 'deep, husky contralto voice, rich chest resonance... speaking at a brisk, punchy, confident clip in her lower register, smiling and energetic without ever sounding shrill or high-pitched', and use periods/commas in setup clauses, reserving '!' for the landing climax.
   - Rising-arc ref_text (the Tail-Energy Rule): Base ICL voice cloning (x_vector_only_mode=False) prepends ref_code and generates new speech tokens immediately after the end of ref_code. Because of causal recency bias, the energy and projection of cloned clips (especially 1-3 s trick/crash calls) are dominated by the final 2-3 seconds of ref_audio. Ending ref_text at peak landing excitement ('...and she stomps the landing clean! Yes, what a run!' / '...and a textbook landing! Clean as you like, write that one down!') gives action lines genuine booth stoke while keeping conversational lines natural.
   - Tighten pauses & avoid 'breathy/never raises her voice': VoiceDesign inserts 350-600 ms pauses and audible sighs when prompted with 'breathy, deadpan, never raises her voice', which ICL cloning copies into game clips. Prompting Wren for 'clear, crisp, agile mezzo voice with a bright, dry, articulate edge—no huskiness and no breathiness' and tightening pauses in design.py ('max_pause_s': 0.14) keeps both announcers brisk and distinct (Dani 248 Hz smoky contralto vs Wren 303 Hz crisp Kiwi mezzo, <= 0.27 similarity to all midnight-playground DJs).

dani.ref_text: Welcome back to the Ten-Eighty Mountain Series, I'm Dani Reyes, and folks, what a run we just saw. Big air off the lip, huge rotation, and she stomps the landing clean! Yes, what a run!

dani-jersey.instruct: A woman around forty-five with a deep, full, round, resonant voice and a thick New Jersey accent, a play-by-play sports announcer with a big heart. Booming and low, great comic timing, stretches words out for drama, laughs from the belly.
dani-jersey.ref_text: Ten-Eighty FM, good morning, mountain. I'm Dani Reyes, and let me tell you something, that last run was really good. Big air, big landing, big heart. Alright, alright. Here comes the next rider. Let's see what you got, babe.

dani-booth.ref_text: Welcome back to the Ten-Eighty Mountain Series! I'm Dani Reyes, and folks, what a run we just saw! Big air, huge rotation, and she sticks the landing! The crowd is on its feet! Here comes the next rider out of the gate, let's see what she's got!

dani-pipe.instruct: A forty-two-year-old woman with a deep, husky contralto voice, rich chest resonance, and a distinct New Jersey accent. A retired pro halfpipe snowboarder calling live TV commentary from the mountain booth: grounded, gravelly, warm and stoked, speaking at a brisk, punchy, confident clip in her lower register, smiling and energetic without ever sounding shrill or high-pitched.
dani-pipe.ref_text: Welcome back to the Ten-Eighty Mountain Series, I'm Dani Reyes, and folks, what a run we just saw. Big air off the lip, huge rotation, and she stomps the landing clean! Yes, what a run!

wren.ref_text: Wren Halvorsen here in the booth. Dani is shouting already, and the snow is running fast today. Watch this line through the rollers, tidy grab, smooth rotation, and a textbook landing! Clean as you like, write that one down!

wren-light.instruct: A small woman in her mid-twenties with a light, high, airy voice and a strong New Zealand accent, a retired racer turned sports commentator. Quick, clipped and deadpan, bone-dry humour, precise diction, a little breathy, never raises her voice.
wren-light.ref_text: This is Ten-Eighty FM. I'm Wren. That was a clean landing, and a very sloppy grab. I'll allow it. Dani is screaming again. We can all hear you, Dani. Next rider. Try to stay on your feet.

wren-booth.ref_text: Wren Halvorsen here in the booth! That was a clean landing, and a very tidy grab. Look at that line, that is textbook! And Dani is shouting again. We can all hear you, Dani! Next rider is in the gate. Here we go!

wren-crisp.instruct: Female sports color analyst in her late twenties with a distinct New Zealand / Southern Hemisphere English accent and non-rhotic pronunciation. Clear, crisp, agile mezzo voice with a bright, dry, articulate edge—no huskiness and no breathiness. Quick-witted retired boardercross racer calling a live snowboard broadcast at a brisk, snappy pace, amused and sharp, finishing with genuine excitement on the landing.
wren-crisp.ref_text: Wren Halvorsen here in the booth. Dani is shouting already, and the snow is running fast today. Watch this line through the rollers, tidy grab, smooth rotation, and a textbook landing! Clean as you like, write that one down!
